ENGINEERING CHECK, 14 Nov 2026 (verified on an emulator against VM 108 updated to sha-4066593, the merge of #53 = frozen commit 40665932; debug APK build 152 from the same commit; NOT the release-candidate pair; nothing is marked walked). N-13 WORKS FOR A PHONE THAT HAS NO ROW FOR THE SONG, AND DOES NOT SHOW FOR THE PHONE THAT TAPPED IT.
SEEN: searched "lofi for focus" (the song the B-117 finding says no search matches). My first tap on the Top result made the server search once and remember `not_found` (song_ref: missing_reason not_found, missing_at = missing_tried_at, matcher revision 1). A second tap 50 s later did NOT search again (missing_tried_at unchanged) and the phone said "Couldn't play Lofi For Focus: Nothing matching that song was found." in under 3 s. The server's own `refs.unavailable_for` answers the live verdict with retryAfter = +7 days. After signing out and in again (a phone with no library row for the song) the same search showed the Top result GREY: "Lofi For Focus / Song - Lofi & Sleep / Not available on your server", a quiet "no entry" circle instead of Play; tapping it did not try (no spinner, nothing queued) and the snackbar said "Nothing matching that song was found. Try again in a few days." That is the drawing (S-12).
NOT SEEN, audit row B-128: on the phone that TAPPED, the song is no longer grey. The tap made the song a row of the phone's library (tracks.is_ref = 1, no file: read from the phone's own database), Search merges that row with the catalogue hit (the Top result got a "..." menu and a normal Play circle), and the mark is read only from the catalogue hit (search_results.dart `_card`, `songMarkProvider(h.catalogue!.id)`), so a library row is never marked. This is the gap the helper disclosed ("library and playlist rows are not marked yet"), here seen in the owner's own scenario: the same person taps an unfindable song and searches again. `Rebuild library` keeps that row (3245 songs before and after). Also: `SongMarks` trusts a "no problem" answer for 10 minutes (`kSongMarksFreshFor`), so a phone that asked BEFORE the tap shows the song playable for up to 10 minutes even with no row; a failed tap does not set the mark itself.
LOOK-UPS: this check spent one tap = one YouTube search flow (up to 3 requests). Search's "prepare" of the Top result is `POST refs/resolve` only (the look-up waits for the tap), proved from `EncoreInstantBackend.prepare`: it made junk rows, not look-ups (audit B-126). Next for this item: mark library and playlist rows (ask by ref id, as the helper planned), set the mark at once when a tap is refused for good, and look at the 10-minute trust. Check first whether a grey library row is drawn.
